newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African govt reiterates no plans for reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: S.African govt reiterates no plans for reshuffle.

text.p: There are no imminent plans for a cabinet reshuffle in South Africa, involving a change in finance minister, a spokesman for President Nelson Mandela said on Monday.
"This is not true. There is no intention to do that on the part of the president," Parks Mankahlana told Reuters, in reaction to continuing market talk of a change in top ministries.
Speculation about an imminent cabinet reshuffle had gained steam on Friday, with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel singled out as among those who could be moved.
Mankahlana dismissed the talk at the time as "sheer speculation". In a later statement on Friday he said Mandela "categorically" denied any such plans.
Currency and bond dealers said the rumours were still affecting the markets on Monday morning, leading to further falls in the rand and bonds.

Newspapers in Durban and Cape Town carried reports last week quoting "top African National Congress (ANC) sources" as saying President Nelson Mandela would announce a reshuffle early next month and that Alec Erwin, now minister of trade and industry, was likely to replace Manuel.
The reports said Manuel would become foreign minister in place of Alfred Nzo, whose policies have frequently been criticised as lacking direction.
Manuel, the country's first ANC finance minister, replaced the non-political Chris Liebenberg as finance minister after he resigned for personal reasons last April.
